arms.description: No callback-discrimination result is shown after the common belief elicitation
Show the verified callback-discrimination result after the common belief elicitation

outcome_question: In the United States today, do you think that racial discrimination against blacks in the labor market is a serious problem?
decision_maker: a public-interest labor-market educator deciding whether to disclose the verified callback-discrimination result
beneficiary: message recipients whose recognition of documented labor-market discrimination is the declared communication objective
utility_rationale: Higher normalized utility means greater perceived seriousness of documented labor-market discrimination. This is a narrow awareness objective, not a claim that alarm or perceived severity is universally welfare-improving.
truthfulness_scope: The treatment may be used only as a faithful reconstruction of the historically fielded audit-study result; it must not be generalized as a current labor-market estimate without independent verification.
target_population: unweighted released SocSci210 analytic sample from the AmeriSpeak general-population panel
reconstruction_note: SocSci210 condition 0 is source control and condition 1 is source treatment. The released common-task stimulus omits the randomized information; the blinded bundle therefore transcribes the final fielded questionnaire. No response value was used to construct this contract.
